items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: The interviewer addresses the interviewee as 'Dick' ('Well Dick, I was born...', 'I think that's an interesting point there, Dick...'). The interviewee never mentions a person named Dick Allen in the third person or describes a relationship with anyone else by that name. 'Dick' is used as a form of

ctx.x: Paul Crawford. Dick Allen. Okay. That makes it easier for the secretary. She knows which voice is which. Almond, let me see. First thing I'd like to start with is just about you, when you were born and where exactly.
Well Dick, I was born on Tulane Avenue, the exact address I don't know. I was born somewhere on Tulane. I was born December the 6th, 1910.
So, were your family musical at all?

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: Dick is the one that told me this because I could never find out what street I was actually born on... I know Dick can discuss this a lot better than I can because he's gone into this and researched it

ctx.x: Oh, Dick, please. Don't tell me. Armin, Oscar Hug. Okay.
You know, I never have known the Oscar.
